texts: When the heart says enough, all the kingdoms of the earth turn to dust beneath its feet.
doha about being happy with just enough, nothing more needed
Please write a doha for a person who has stopped chasing a bigger salary and a bigger life, and found that a simple meal and a quiet evening are all the richness the heart ever required.
After years of overtime I finally turned down the promotion, and sitting at home with dal and rice and my family I felt richer than ever.
enough is plenty
doha on a pot of water and a simple meal, being happy with just enough
Write a doha about a person who sits with a plain meal and a pot of water by his side, wanting nothing more, and who feels that kings with all their treasure could not match his peace.
pot of water, enough
A pot of water, a crust of bread, and a heart that asks for nothing more, and all the treasure of the world is dust.
On my morning walk I saw a labourer drinking from his pot of water in the shade with a face so calm that I envied him his whole lot.
need a doha for someone who wants more and more, tell them enough is enough
My friend has a good job, a lovely family and a nice flat, yet keeps feeling he lacks something; I wish someone would tell him he has had enough all along.

Please compose a doha about the peace that arrives the moment a person stops comparing and says the plain words, this much is enough for me, and finds all earthly riches turning to dust before that peace.
When the heart is full of its own enough, the richest king is a pauper by comparison.
satisfied with enough
I used to chase a bigger car and a bigger title, but when I started being satisfied with my daily bread and a clear conscience, nothing else seemed to matter. Write a doha capturing that peace.
O soul that has said enough, you are a king without a crown, and all the wealth of the world is a handful of dust to you.
My mother has never owned much, but she hums while cooking the same simple dinner, and the richest people I know look at her with envy.
doha about being fine with what you have
just enough, at peace
moon, enough
Lying on the roof with a simple blanket and the moon above, I realised I didn't need anything more than this, and that all the rest I'd been chasing was noise.
Write a doha about a person sitting under the moon with just a plain meal and a quiet mind, feeling that all the money in the world would add nothing to what he already holds in peace.
The moon asks for no crown and no cushion, yet she rules the night; so the heart that wants no more is king.
doha with the moon, about being happy with what you have
date palm, cloth sheet, enough
doha on sleeping under a date palm on a cloth sheet and needing nothing else
After the long trip I laid down a cloth sheet under a date palm and slept better than I had in any expensive bed, and the thought stayed with me for months.
A cloth sheet spread beneath the date palm is a throne to the one who wants nothing more.
Compose a doha where a man rests on a simple cloth sheet beneath a date palm, satisfied with the shade and the fruit, and he feels richer than the owner of any estate because the wanting has stopped.
pls write a doha about being satisfied and not wanting more
My grandfather sat on the porch each evening with his tea and said, what more could a man ask for; I would like a doha in his spirit.

Please write a doha for someone who has come to see that having a little and wanting no more is the greatest fortune, and that riches, once the craving ends, turn to dust in the hands of the satisfied.
peace in enough
When desire lays down its burden, the poor man's little overflows and the rich man's plenty looks dry.
doha about a beggar who is more satisfied than a king
beggar, perfect satisfaction
A beggar outside our colony always smiles even when given only a little, while my neighbour with three cars never seems to be happy at all.
Write a doha about a beggar who takes whatever is given, thanks the giver, and sleeps soundly, contrasted with the rich man who wants more every day and never enjoys what he has.
The beggar's bowl is half empty and his face is full of peace; the king's vault is full and his eyes are hungry.
doha with rope and a spinning wheel, being happy with a simple life
rope, spinning wheel, enough
My grandmother twists rope from jute on her spinning wheel and asks for nothing more from life than the day's work and the evening's rest; I'd love a doha on her.
Compose a doha where an old woman works at her spinning wheel, twisting a simple rope, content with what each day brings, and the whole wealth of the world is dust to her satisfied heart.
The wheel turns, the rope grows, the day is full, and the heart that asks for nothing more holds the world.
Enough is the seat on which the contented rest, and they look upon the ambitions of the greedy with a smile.
satisfied, needing nothing
When my father retired he said he'd finally learned that what he had was already plenty, and he laughs more now than he ever did at the office.
Please write a doha about the quiet joy of living on what one has, without envying the neighbour or counting the savings, in which riches are seen for the dust they truly are.
doha about how having enough makes you rich
The lion needs no hoard and no crown, and the mark on the wise man's forehead asks for nothing; they are the kings of enough.
lion, forehead mark, enough
At the village festival, the old man with a mark on his forehead ate his simple food and said it was more than a lion's feast; that content face stays with me.

Write a doha where a lion rests content after its meal, with no thought of the next, and an old wise man with a mark on his forehead is just as satisfied, showing kings' riches are dust beside this peace.
doha on a lion and a forehead mark, about being satisfied with enough
In the mosque courtyard the faithful sit with simple bread and a quiet heart, and the treasure of kings is dust to them.

Please write a doha about a person who sits in the mosque after prayers, satisfied with the little God has given, wanting nothing more, and who finds all the wealth of the world dust before the peace that satisfaction brings.
doha about being thankful and satisfied, mosque in it
mosque, contentment's peace
At the mosque near my office there is a man who sells nothing, begs for nothing, and each Friday simply sits smiling; I have never met anyone so full.
doha on a palace and a bitter gourd, being fine with what you have

A king in his palace is restless and wants more, while a poor man eats a plain meal of bitter gourd and sleeps in peace; please write a doha about the one who is truly wealthy through being satisfied.
palace, bitter gourd, enough
The palace is full of wanting, the bitter gourd on the poor man's plate is sweet with enough.
After visiting a huge palace on a school trip, my father ate his simple bitter gourd curry at home that night and said he would not trade it for any of that.
doha about rope and spinning wheel and being happy with simple things
My aunt, who spins her own rope on a little wheel, once refused a nice gift saying she already had all she needs; write a doha for her.

Write a doha on a woman at her spinning wheel making rope for the day's needs, wanting nothing more, and showing that the wealth of the greedy is dust beside the peace of someone satisfied with a modest day.
The wheel hums, the rope coils, and the heart that wants no more is richer than the lord of a thousand fields.
spinning wheel, rope, enough
My brother swapped his sword-fighting hobby for a quiet life on a boat in a fishing village and says he has never been so satisfied with so little.
A warrior puts down his sword and sits on a small boat with a simple meal, satisfied with the day, and realises that the fame he chased was dust beside this quiet peace. Please write a doha for that.
The sword is sheathed, the boat drifts, and the heart that wants no more sails over every kingdom.
sword, boat, satisfied heart
doha with a sword and a boat, being happy with just enough
The river runs on without a crown, and the bird in the cage sings for a bowl of grain; blessed is the one whose enough is like theirs.
doha with a river and a cage, about being okay with what you have
Sitting by the river, I saw a pet bird in a little cage singing happily for its seeds, and I wondered why I, who have so much more, always feel I need something else.
Please compose a doha about someone resting by a river beside an empty cage, no longer wanting to own or add, and finding that this plain peace outweighs all the wealth the world offers.
river, cage, enough
doha on bitter gourd and being satisfied, simple food simple life
Bitter gourd on a plain plate tastes sweet to the heart that wants no more.
bitter gourd, content

Write a doha about a poor family sharing a meal of bitter gourd, thankful for what they have, whose happiness could not be bought by all the riches of the powerful, because satisfaction is richer than money.
My mother cooked bitter gourd for dinner for the fifth day in a row, and nobody complained, we were just glad to be sitting together.
doha about a lion and a yogi, being satisfied with enough
The lion lies down after its meal and does not hunt, and the yogi eats his handful of rice; both are kings of enough.

A yogi sits among the trees eating only what comes, and nearby a lion rests content after its meal; please write a doha showing that all the riches of cities are dust compared with the peace of such satisfaction.
A yogi once told me that a lion never takes more than it needs, and I realised I'd spent my whole life taking more than I needed.
lion, yogi, enough
My cousin spent years casting a net of side jobs to catch more income and ended up exhausted, until he quietly dropped them all and was happier with less.

Please write a doha about a fisherman who stops casting his net wider and wider, content with the day's catch, and finds more peace in being satisfied than in all the riches that more fishing could bring.
net, enough
doha about a net and being happy with what you caught
The net rests on the shore, the heart rests in its enough, and the tide of wanting grows still.
I looked at a photograph of a peacock beside a skeleton in a museum and thought about how little a person needs while alive, since nothing at all goes with us; I want a doha on being satisfied.
skeleton, peacock, enough
doha with a skeleton and a peacock, about being satisfied with what you have
Write a doha where a peacock dances happily with nothing but its feathers, and beside it a skeleton rests with nothing at all, to show that satisfaction with enough is the only wealth that is real.
The peacock dances on its own feathers, the skeleton wants for nothing, and between the two sits the wise one who has said enough.
snake, lock, enough
The snake sleeps without a lock to guard its hole, and the heart that wants no more sleeps as peacefully.
doha with a snake and a lock, about being satisfied and not hoarding
We hardly lock up at night since we own so little, and the snake in our garden seems to like it as much as we do; I'd like a doha on that.
Write a doha where a snake lies calmly with no lock and no hoard, while the rich man bolts his gates, showing that the peace of enough is worth more than all the wealth that needs a lock.
ash, thread, enough
Ash on the brow, a thread around the wrist, and a heart that asks for nothing, the richest of all men.
My uncle wears a sacred thread and smears ash on his forehead every morning, owns almost nothing, and says he has had more than enough of everything.
Please compose a doha about a wanderer with ash on his body and a simple thread, satisfied with what he is given, and for whom the wealth of kings is only dust beside his peace.
doha with ash and thread, about being happy with a simple life
gold, snake, enough
Write a doha where gold lies in a heap and a snake coils upon it, restless and watchful, while a poor man sleeps soundly with nothing, showing that satisfaction makes gold into dust.
The snake coils upon the gold and never rests, while the poor man with nothing sleeps like a king.
A jeweller friend of mine counts gold all day and is full of worries, while his old neighbour, who owns almost nothing, sleeps in the courtyard like a snake in the warmth without a care.
doha with gold and a snake, being content with less
A single cloth sheet spread on the floor is a bed for the one who wants no more, softer than any velvet of kings.
doha about a cloth sheet and being content with a simple bed
cloth sheet, enough
We had to sleep on a cloth sheet on the floor the first week in our new town, and strangely those were the happiest nights we have known.
Write a doha where a man lies on a plain cloth sheet, with nothing more than the day's meal inside him, and sleeps more soundly than any king, because the end of wanting is the real wealth.
needing nothing more
When my daughter said she didn't want a bigger room because she liked hers just as it is, I felt a pride I couldn't explain.
Wherever the heart says enough, a royal welcome is spread, and every wealth of the world is a pinch of dust.
Please write a doha about the shift that happens inside when you stop asking life for more, and instead sit with what you have, feeling that all the money in the world has become simply dust.
write a doha about being happy with enough please
A thorn in the path is still a small price when the heart has said enough, for the satisfied walk without pain.
doha with a thorn in it, being content even when life is rough
thorn, enough
I walked barefoot on a rough path at my village last summer, stepped on a thorn, and still felt happier than I do in my air-conditioned flat.
Write a doha about a poor traveller walking a thorny path who is nonetheless satisfied, and whose peace of mind is richer than the wealth of those who ride in comfort but always want more.
The tree gives shade without asking for anything, and the heart that has enough sits under it, richer than a king.
Please write a doha about someone resting beneath a tree with a handful of rice and no thought of tomorrow, whose satisfaction makes all the wealth of the world seem like dust that blows away.
We spent a whole weekend under an old tree by the farm with nothing but dal-roti, and I was happier than at any resort we have ever paid for.
tree, enough
doha with a tree in it, about being satisfied with what you have
pearl, swan, enough
The swan needs no pearl to know its worth, and the heart that wants no more finds all riches dust.
My aunt, who gave away her pearl necklace and walks as gracefully as a swan in her simple saree, says she has never felt wealthier.
Write a doha about a swan gliding without wanting the pearls beneath the surface, satisfied with the water and the day, and showing that when contentment arrives every riches is dust.
doha on a pearl and a swan, being happy with enough

A washerman scrubs clothes at the edge of the temple tank all day, earns little, sings in the evening and sleeps soundly, while rich worshippers inside still pray for more. Please write a doha on this.
doha with a washerman and a temple, about being happy with a simple life
The washerman sings at the temple's edge, wanting for nothing, while the rich pray inside for more.
Every morning on my way to the temple I pass a washerman who whistles at his work, and I realise I've never whistled at mine.
washerman, temple, enough
Enough is a quiet country where no ruler is needed, and where silver and coin are only dust underfoot.
Please compose a doha about the moment a person realises that the comforts they already have are all they ever needed, and that every effort to add more was only a restless illusion that falls away.
I have enough
At forty I deleted all the shopping apps from my phone and noticed, for the first time in years, that nothing in my life was missing.
doha about being happy with what you already have
My uncle's tongue was always asking for more, more profit, more praise, until one day a quiet illness taught him the taste of simple bread.
Please write a doha about the tongue that once asked for rich food and sweet praise, and which now, learning satisfaction, is happy with plain rice and silence, because it has finally found enough.
doha about tongue craving and being satisfied with plain food
tongue, enough
The tongue that sought a thousand flavours is at peace with bread, and in that peace all treasure is dust.
Crossing the bridge to our village each evening, I see a crow on the railing and a farmer walking home with a simple meal, and both look more complete than most people I know.
The crow on the bridge needs no kingdom, the farmer crossing needs no crown; both are rich in enough.
bridge, crow, enough
Write a doha where a crow rests on a bridge with no wish for more, and the people crossing hurry by chasing gains, showing that the one who is satisfied owns the greatest riches of all.
doha with a bridge and a crow, about being happy with enough
doha about being content with whatever god gives

Please write a doha for a person who has spent years running after one more thing and now sits quietly with a simple meal, understanding that satisfaction is a wealth no robber can take and no king can buy.
When my friend's lottery ticket didn't win, he laughed and said he already had everything he could use anyway, and I envied the lightness in his voice.
satisfied heart
The heart that has said enough has found a shelter that no storm can touch.
doha with a bier and a mosque, how enough is all we need
Walking past a mosque I saw a bier being carried out, and it struck me that nothing but the simple cloth went with him; I want a doha on being satisfied with enough.
Write a doha where a bier is carried past a mosque, reminding everyone that the world's wealth cannot travel, while the satisfied man who wanted only enough has lost nothing and gained peace.
At the mosque gate the bier passes, and none carries more than a plain cloth; blessed is he who wanted no more.
bier, mosque, enough
At the loom the weaver sings, for he asks for no more than the day's bread, and the wealth of kings is dust to him.
doha with a weaver's loom, about being happy with enough
weaver's loom, enough
Please write a doha about a weaver at his loom who earns just enough for the day, lives without envy, and finds that no hoard in a rich man's chest can match the peace he carries home at evening.
My neighbour works his old loom from dawn, wants nothing beyond the day's food, and his family is the happiest in our street.
A leaf trembles on the tree and asks nothing of the sky; so rests the heart that has found enough.
leaf, tree, enough
Write a doha about a leaf on a tree that wants nothing beyond the morning light and the breeze, and compare this peace with the restless man who owns whole orchards but is never satisfied.
doha with a leaf and a tree, being fine with what you have
I watched one leaf come down from the tree in our yard this morning while I sipped my tea, and felt no urge for anything else in the world.
doha about being okay with little
My sister quit her high-paying consulting job to teach in a village school and says she has never felt so full with so little.
Little is plenty to the heart that is full, and plenty is little to the heart that wants.

Please write a doha about the strange fact that those with the least often feel richest, because they've stopped asking for more, while the wealthy keep searching for a satisfaction that is already within them.
little, yet whole
doha about being content, nothing more to ask for
When desire is still, the whole world's treasure is a handful of dust.
I'd like a doha for the evening of life, when one sits with a cup of tea and family and no longer asks for more, and where every earthly fortune seems like a pile of dust beside this calm.
After my father retired and sold the second car, he said it was the first year he never felt anything was lacking.
enough, at last
The tree stands in its own shade and asks for nothing, the traveller who rests there is richer than any lord.
Please write a doha about an old tree and the man who sits beneath it with no more than he needs, and who feels richer than the owner of a great estate because he has stopped wanting.
doha with a tree about being satisfied with what you've got
The old tree outside our gate gives shade to anyone, and the man who sits under it each afternoon with his lunch box seems to own the world.
tree, satisfied heart
doha with ash in it, about being happy with nothing much
Ash on the brow and bread on the plate, and a heart that asks for nothing: this is richer than any king.
Write a doha about a wandering renunciant whose body is covered with ash, who accepts only what is offered, and who is happier than rich people because he has stopped wanting anything more.
My uncle gave away most of his belongings, smears ash on his forehead each morning, and when I ask how he is, says, I have more than enough.
ash, satisfied heart
Dew on the grass at dawn is enough for the thirsty morning, and a mark on the brow is enough for a devout heart.
dew, forehead mark, enough
Early in the morning my grandmother touches the dew on the grass and then the mark on her own forehead, saying that is all the blessing she needs.
doha with dew and a forehead mark, being satisfied with simple things

Please compose a doha about a person who rises at dawn, touches the dew and wears the mark on his forehead, wants nothing from the world, and in that simple morning finds a satisfaction that outweighs all riches.
My neighbour's children play with a ball and an old tyre in the lane and laugh louder than my kids with their new gadgets ever do.
Joy is born where wanting dies, and the humblest home outshines the grandest.
needing less
doha for kids and elders who are happy with what they have

Please write a doha about the way a heart becomes full the moment it stops comparing itself to others, and how all the riches of the neighbour, the cousin, and the king become dust before that fullness.

I want a doha for a woman who works hard for her family, has a modest home and simple dreams, and who now understands that all the extra money in the world would change nothing in the peace she holds.
no craving, no lack
doha on being at peace with what you earn
Last Diwali we spent very little and still the evening felt complete, and my wife said it was the best one we had had in years.
Where the heart has no more asking, every day is a celebration and every meal a banquet.
My grandfather sat every evening under the tree by the well drinking his tea and saying he had everything; I always felt that was a kind of kingship.
Write a doha about a man resting under a tree beside a well, content with the day's meal and a drink of cool water, who has everything a king could want because he wants nothing more.
doha with a tree and a well, about being happy with enough
tree, well, enough
A tree for shade, a well for water, and a heart for peace: these three are all the kingdom a man needs.
The snake guards no pearl and the poor man owns none, yet the poor man sleeps sound; enough is the finest treasure.
doha with a snake and a pearl, being content with enough
snake, pearl, enough
Compose a doha where a snake coils around a pearl that a greedy man longs for, while a satisfied man passes by without a glance, because to him the world's treasure is only dust.
A rich collector once showed me a pearl guarded by a snake-carved box, and then I met a fisherman who had neither, and he was the happier man.
contentment is wealth
When the heart says enough, a thousand treasures become a handful of dust.
doha about being fine with enough
Please write a doha for a retired teacher who lives on a small pension, owns little, and who says she has never lacked anything, because she has long since learned to be satisfied with enough.
My aunt lives on a tiny pension, has no luxuries, and still hosts everyone with a smile and says she has all she needs.
doha with a churn, about being content with simple butter and bread

Please write a doha about a village woman who turns her churn at dawn, takes only the buttermilk and bread her family needs, and finds that she is richer than the wealthy because she wants nothing more.
Each morning my grandmother works the churn and says the day's food is enough, and she never worries about tomorrow, and I would like a doha in that spirit.
churn, enough
The churn turns, the butter comes, and the heart that asks no more has all the kingdom of the world.
doha with a bridge and a furnace, being happy with what you have
My uncle works near a furnace under the bridge, comes home sooty and tired, and is still the most satisfied man I know when he sits down to his dinner.
The furnace burns for the wanting and the bridge leads to the next desire, but the one who has said enough stays still.

Write a doha where a furnace roars with the world's craving and a bridge carries people toward more, while one man who has found enough stands aside at peace, and every fortune turns to dust before him.
bridge, furnace, enough
A fish swims in the same pond all its life and never longs for the wide world beyond, and a man is happy with his little field; please write a doha for those who find enough where they are.
My grandfather has fished in the same pond for forty years and never once wished to try another, and always comes home with a smile.
The fish loves its pond as the king loves his realm, and finds it just as wide, for the heart that wants no more has no edges.
doha about a fish and being satisfied with what you have
fish, enough
A yogi once told me, while we watched the moon rise over our village, that the moon needs nothing and yet lights up everything, and that this is what being satisfied looks like.
Write a doha where a yogi sits beneath the moon with no belongings, satisfied with the silence and the night, and the wealth of kings is dust beside the peace he carries.
doha with a yogi and the moon, about being content
yogi, moon, enough
The yogi and the moon share one quiet, neither wants a crown, and both are richer than all the lords of the earth.
